name: Kongo Expansion under Lukeni lua Nimi
description: Traditional account of the conquests by Kongo's founder figure that consolidated the kingdom from its Mpemba Kasi nucleus across the lower Congo.

name: Kongo Civil War of 1506
description: Succession war in which the Christian prince Mvemba a Nzinga (Afonso I) defeated his pagan half-brother Mpanzu a Kitima at the Battle of Mbanza Kongo, securing the throne and the Portuguese alliance.

name: Kongo-Ndongo War of 1556
description: Defeat of Kongo forces by the Ngola of Ndongo that effectively ended Kongo's claim to suzerainty south of the Dande River.

name: Jaga Invasion of Kongo
description: Devastating invasion by the Jaga that drove King Alvaro I from Mbanza Kongo and was reversed only by a Portuguese expeditionary force under Francisco de Gouveia Sottomaior in 1574.

name: Portuguese Conquest of Angola
description: Century-long Portuguese campaign of conquest beginning with Paulo Dias de Novais's 1575 expedition and culminating with the destruction of Kongo at Mbwila and Soyo at Kitombo.

name: Battle of Massangano
description: Portuguese victory over Ndongo forces on the Kwanza River that secured the inland presidio of Massangano as the base for further conquest.

name: Battle of the Lukala
description: Decisive defeat of governor Luis Serrao's Portuguese-Imbangala column by a Ndongo-Matamba coalition that halted Portuguese expansion for a generation.

name: Imbangala Invasions
description: Series of campaigns by the Imbangala warrior bands across the Angolan plateau that destabilised Ndongo and supplied slaves to Portuguese Luanda, eventually settling as the Kasanje kingdom.

name: Portuguese-Ndongo War of 1618-1621
description: Campaigns of Governor Luis Mendes de Vasconcelos that, allied with Imbangala bands, sacked the Ndongo royal capital of Kabasa and forced King Ngola Mbandi onto an island in the Kwanza.

name: Battle of Mbumbi
description: Portuguese-Imbangala raid into Kongo's Mbamba province that defeated and killed the Marquis of Mbumbi, triggering Kongo's first major war against Portugal.

name: Battle of Mbanda Kasi
description: Kongolese victory under King Pedro II that drove Portuguese forces out of southern Kongo following the Mbumbi raid.

name: Portuguese-Njinga Wars
description: Three decades of guerrilla and conventional warfare led by Queen Njinga Mbande against Portuguese Angola, ending with the 1656 peace treaty that recognised her sovereignty in Matamba.

name: Battle of Kavanga
description: Portuguese defeat of Queen Njinga's forces in which her sister Kambu (Barbara) was captured, prompting Njinga's diplomatic appeal to Kongo and the Dutch.

name: Dutch Conquest of Luanda
description: Dutch West India Company capture and seven-year occupation of Luanda during the Dutch-Portuguese War, ended by Salvador de Sa's relief expedition from Brazil.

name: Battle of Kombi
description: Major victory of Njinga's allied Dutch-Kongo-Matamba army over the Portuguese in the Dande valley that nearly ended Portuguese rule in Angola.

name: Recapture of Luanda
description: Salvador Correia de Sa's amphibious assault from Brazil that recaptured Luanda from the Dutch and restored Portuguese control of Angola.

name: Kongo-Portuguese War of 1622
description: Brief but sharp war between Kongo under Pedro II and Portuguese Angola, ending in a Kongolese strategic victory and Portuguese withdrawal.

name: Battle of Mbwila
description: Catastrophic Kongo defeat in which King Antonio I was killed by Portuguese-led forces, shattering the unitary monarchy and inaugurating the Kongo Civil War.

name: Kongo Civil War
description: Forty-four years of dynastic conflict among the Kimpanzu, Kinlaza and Kimulaza branches of the Kongo royal house, ending with Pedro IV's reunification at the Battle of Mbula.

name: Battle of Kitombo
description: Decisive Soyo victory over a Portuguese invasion force under Joao Soares de Almeida that effectively ended Portuguese designs on northern Kongo for two centuries.

name: Antonian Movement
description: Prophetic Christian uprising led by Dona Beatriz Kimpa Vita to reunify Kongo under a restored Mbanza Kongo, crushed when she was burned at the stake by Pedro IV's faction.

name: Battle of Mbula
description: Pedro IV's victory over the Kinlaza faction that ended the Kongo Civil War and restored a federated monarchy at Mbanza Kongo.

name: Lunda Expansion under Mwaant Yaav
description: Century of conquests by the Mwaant Yaav rulers that built the Lunda Empire from its Musumba core across the savanna between the Kwango and the Luapula.

name: Kazembe Conquests
description: Eastward Lunda offshoot under Mwata Kazembe that subdued the peoples of the Luapula valley and established the kingdom that later met Portuguese envoys from Tete.

name: Luba Empire Expansion under Kalala Ilunga
description: Conquests traditionally credited to Kalala Ilunga that built the Luba kingdom around the Upemba lakes by overthrowing Nkongolo Mwamba.

name: Yaka-Kongo Wars
description: Recurring raids by the Yaka of the Kwango against Kongo's eastern provinces, contributing to the demographic drain of the slave trade era.

name: Kasanje Wars
description: Recurring Imbangala-descended Kasanje conflicts with Portuguese Angola and Matamba over control of the slave-trading feiras of the Kwango.

name: Portuguese-Matamba War of 1744
description: Portuguese punitive expedition that defeated Queen Ana II of Matamba and reasserted vassalage of the kingdom to Luanda.

name: Portuguese-Kongo War of 1670
description: Portuguese campaign against Soyo to enforce trade demands, ending in catastrophic defeat at Kitombo.

name: Loango Expansion
description: Period in which the Vili kingdom of Loango extended its commercial empire along the north Congo coast, projecting power into Kakongo, Ngoyo and Mayombe.

name: Tio-Bobangi Conflicts
description: Slow displacement of Tio commercial dominance on the Malebo Pool by the Bobangi river traders during the height of the Atlantic and Congo-basin slave trades.

name: Chokwe Expansion
description: Chokwe mercenary and slave-raiding expansion out of the Angolan highlands that overran the Lunda heartland in the 1880s and toppled the Mwaant Yaav.

name: Msiri's Wars
description: Conquests of the Nyamwezi warlord Msiri that built the Yeke Kingdom in Katanga, ended by his killing at Bunkeya by Captain Stairs's Congo Free State expedition.

name: Portuguese-Dembos Wars
description: Half-century of intermittent Portuguese campaigns to subdue the Dembos chiefdoms north of Luanda, finally completed only during World War I.

name: Bailundo War
description: Major Ovimbundu uprising on the Benguela plateau led by King Mutu-ya-Kevela against Portuguese rubber-trade abuses, crushed by Lieutenant-Colonel Joao de Almeida's columns.

name: Kwanyama Wars
description: Series of Portuguese campaigns against the Kwanyama of the Angolan-Namibian border, ending with the killing of King Mandume ya Ndemufayo and the partition of Ovamboland.

name: Battle of Mufilo
description: Portuguese defeat by Kwanyama forces under Mandume during the early phase of the Ovamboland campaigns.

name: Battle of Mongua
description: Portuguese victory under General Pereira de Eca that broke Kwanyama resistance and completed the conquest of southern Angola.

name: Bakongo Revolt of 1913-1914
description: Last armed Kongo uprising against Portuguese rule, led by Manuel Kiditu and Alvaro Buta, crushed in 1914 and effectively ending the Kongo monarchy.

name: Portuguese-German Border War in Angola
description: Frontier clashes between German South West Africa and Portuguese Angola, including the German victory at Naulila and the subsequent Kwanyama uprising.

name: Belgian Conquest of Congo Free State
description: Force Publique conquest of the Congo basin under Leopold II's personal rule, accompanied by mass atrocities in the rubber and ivory zones.

name: Congo Arab War
description: Two-year Force Publique campaign under Francis Dhanis that destroyed the Swahili-Arab slave-trading network of Tippu Tip in the eastern Congo.

name: Batetela Mutiny of 1895
description: First mutiny of Tetela soldiers in the Force Publique garrison at Luluabourg, triggered by the execution of Chief Gongo Lutete and sustained as a low-level revolt across the Kasai.

name: Batetela Mutiny of 1897
description: Second Batetela mutiny in Dhanis's Nile expedition force, which fled to the forests of the eastern Congo and was hunted for three years by Force Publique columns.

name: Boma Mutiny
description: Brief Force Publique mutiny at the Free State capital of Boma, suppressed within days.

name: Yaka War
description: Force Publique campaign to subdue the Yaka chiefdoms of the Kwango plateau, characterised by heavy reprisals against rubber-collecting villages.

name: Lulonga and Mongala Revolts
description: Recurring revolts in the Equateur rubber concessions of the Lulonga, Mongala and Maringa basins, suppressed by ABIR and Anversoise sentries with mass killings.

name: Pende Revolt
description: Pende uprising against forced palm-oil cultivation and the Huileries du Congo Belge in the Kwilu, suppressed by Force Publique with hundreds killed.

name: Kuba Revolts
description: Kuba resistance to Compagnie du Kasai rubber collection under King Kot aPe, suppressed by Force Publique punitive expeditions.

name: Kongo-Wara Rebellion
description: Multi-ethnic 'War of the Hoe Handle' against French rubber and porterage demands in Ubangi-Shari and Middle Congo, led by the prophet Karinou and suppressed with thousands killed.

name: French Conquest of Chad
description: Decade-long French campaigns under Lamy, Gentil and Largeau that destroyed Rabih az-Zubayr's empire and conquered Baguirmi, Kanem and Ouaddai.

name: Battle of Kousseri
description: Convergence of the Voulet-Chanoine, Foureau-Lamy and Gentil missions to defeat and kill the warlord Rabih az-Zubayr south of Lake Chad.

name: French Conquest of Ouaddai
description: Colonel Largeau's campaign that captured Abeche, deposed Sultan Doudmourrah and incorporated Ouaddai into French Chad.

name: German Conquest of Kamerun
description: Two decades of Schutztruppe campaigns that subdued the Duala coast, the Bakweri of Mount Cameroon, the Adamawa Fulani and the Grassfields chiefdoms.

name: Bakweri Wars
description: German campaigns against the Bakweri of Mount Cameroon under King Kuva of Buea, ending in 1894 with Kuva's defeat and Buea's destruction.

name: Bafut Wars
description: Three German Schutztruppe expeditions against Fon Abumbi I of Bafut in the Cameroon Grassfields, ending in the burning of the palace and Bafut's submission.

name: Nso War
description: German Schutztruppe campaign against the Fon of Nso in the Grassfields, marked by the killing of Captain Glauning at Kumbo.

name: Kamerun Campaign
description: Anglo-French invasion and conquest of German Kamerun in the First World War, ending with the German surrender at Mora in February 1916.

name: Battle of Garua
description: Anglo-French capture of the German fortified post at Garua on the Benue River, opening the way to the conquest of northern Kamerun.

name: Siege of Mora
description: Eighteen-month Allied siege of the German Schutztruppe garrison on Mora Mountain, the last German position in Kamerun to surrender.

name: Simba Rebellion
description: Lumumbist Simba uprising that briefly held the eastern Congo and Stanleyville, ended by Belgian paratroopers in Operation Dragon Rouge and ANC counter-offensives.

name: Kwilu Rebellion
description: Pierre Mulele's Maoist insurgency in the Kwilu region, which preceded and overlapped with the Simba rebellion in the east.

name: Operation Dragon Rouge
description: Belgian paratrooper rescue operation airlifted by the United States that freed European hostages from Simba-held Stanleyville.

name: Mercenaries' Mutiny
description: Revolt of Jean Schramme's white mercenaries and Katangese gendarmes at Stanleyville and Bukavu against Mobutu, ended by their evacuation to Rwanda.

name: Angolan War of Independence
description: Thirteen-year war by the MPLA, FNLA and UNITA against Portuguese rule in Angola, ending with the Carnation Revolution and the Alvor Accords.

name: Baixa de Cassanje Revolt
description: Cotton-pickers' strike in Portuguese Angola crushed by aerial bombing and ground sweeps, conventionally treated as the start of the Angolan War of Independence.

name: UPA March 1961 Uprising
description: UPA (later FNLA) uprising across northern Angola's coffee plantations, with mass killings of settlers and Ovimbundu workers and a Portuguese reprisal campaign.

name: Cabinda Insurgency
description: Long-running low-intensity insurgency by FLEC factions in the Cabinda exclave demanding independence from Angola.

name: South African Border War in Angola
description: South African Defence Force operations into southern Angola against SWAPO and FAPLA, culminating in the Battle of Cuito Cuanavale and the Tripartite Accord.

name: Battle of Cuito Cuanavale
description: Largest battle in Africa since World War II, fought between FAPLA-Cuban forces and SADF-UNITA on the Lomba River and around Cuito Cuanavale, ending in a strategic stalemate that produced the Namibian-Angolan settlement.

name: Operation Savannah
description: South African armoured intervention in Angola at independence in support of UNITA and the FNLA, halted by Cuban reinforcements south of Luanda.

name: Battle of Quifangondo
description: MPLA-Cuban defeat of the FNLA-Zairean column north of Luanda on the eve of Angolan independence, securing the capital for the MPLA.

name: Shaba I Invasion
description: Invasion of Mobutu's Shaba province by FNLC Katangese exiles from Angola, repulsed by Moroccan troops airlifted by France.

name: Shaba II Invasion
description: Second FNLC incursion that captured Kolwezi and massacred European miners, ended by the French Foreign Legion's parachute drop and Belgian para-commando operations.

name: First Congo War
description: Rwandan-Ugandan-backed AFDL campaign under Laurent-Desire Kabila that toppled Mobutu and ended thirty-two years of Zairean rule.

name: Second Congo War
description: Africa's deadliest war since 1945, drawing in nine states and dozens of militias across the eastern Congo and ending with the Sun City agreement and the transitional government.

name: Six-Day War of Kisangani
description: Urban battle between Rwandan and Ugandan forces in the streets of Kisangani during the Second Congo War, the most intense direct clash between the two RPF-aligned allies.

name: Ituri Conflict
description: Hema-Lendu ethnic war in northeastern Congo's Ituri district during and after the Second Congo War, with major MONUC and EU Operation Artemis interventions.

name: Operation Artemis
description: European Union's first autonomous out-of-area military operation, deployed to stabilise Bunia during the Ituri conflict.

name: Kivu Conflict
description: Ongoing constellation of insurgencies in the eastern Congo following the Second Congo War, including the CNDP, M23, FDLR, ADF and a hundred local Mai-Mai groups.

name: CNDP Insurgency
description: Laurent Nkunda's Tutsi-led CNDP rebellion in North Kivu, ended by the Rwanda-DRC Goma agreement and Nkunda's arrest.

name: M23 Rebellion
description: Rwandan-backed ex-CNDP mutiny that captured Goma in 2012, collapsed in 2013, and reemerged from 2021 as the dominant insurgent threat in the eastern Congo.

name: Allied Democratic Forces Insurgency
description: Long-running Ugandan-origin Islamist insurgency operating across the Rwenzori border, increasingly linked since 2019 to the Islamic State Central Africa Province.

name: FDLR Insurgency
description: Hutu militia descended from the ex-FAR and Interahamwe based in the eastern Congo, targeted by repeated FARDC, Rwandan and UN operations.

name: Kamuina Nsapu Rebellion
description: Customary chieftaincy-based militia uprising in the Kasai region against Kinshasa, marked by mass atrocities and the killing of two UN experts.

name: CODECO Insurgency
description: Lendu-aligned cooperative militia in Ituri responsible for major massacres of Hema civilians and persistent fighting with FARDC and ADF.

name: Bas-Congo Bundu dia Kongo Clashes
description: Police and army crackdowns on the Bundu dia Kongo revivalist movement in Bas-Congo, with hundreds of adherents killed.

name: Republic of the Congo Civil War of 1993-1994
description: Post-election clashes between militias loyal to Pascal Lissouba, Bernard Kolelas and Denis Sassou Nguesso in Brazzaville.

name: Republic of the Congo Civil War of 1997-1999
description: Civil war in which Sassou Nguesso's Cobra militia, backed by Angolan intervention, ousted President Lissouba and seized Brazzaville.

name: Pool War
description: Insurgency by Pastor Ntumi's Ninja militia in the Pool region south of Brazzaville, with a renewed 2016-2017 phase.

name: Equatorial Guinea Coups
description: Pattern of coups and coup attempts in Equatorial Guinea, including Obiang's 1979 takeover of Macias Nguema and the 2004 Mark Thatcher Wonga Coup attempt.

name: Sao Tome Coups
description: Series of brief and bloodless coups in Sao Tome and Principe, including the 1995 and 2003 takeovers by army officers later reversed by negotiation.

name: Gabonese 1964 Coup
description: Brief coup against President Leon Mba reversed by French paratroopers under Operation Bata, an early example of the post-colonial Francafrique military doctrine.

name: Central African Republic Bush War
description: Northern CAR rebellion by the UFDR and APRD against Francois Bozize, eased by the 2007 Birao peace agreement.

name: Central African Republic Civil War
description: Seleka coalition's overthrow of Francois Bozize, the rise of Anti-balaka self-defence militias, and the protracted communal war that drew in France's Operation Sangaris, MINUSCA and the Wagner Group.

name: Seleka Offensive
description: Seleka rebel coalition's southward march from northern CAR that captured Bangui in March 2013 and installed Michel Djotodia as president.

name: Anti-balaka Campaign
description: Christian and animist self-defence militias' offensive against ex-Seleka and Muslim civilians across western CAR, with major atrocities in Bangui and Bossangoa.

name: Operation Sangaris
description: French military intervention in the CAR alongside MISCA and MINUSCA to halt the Seleka-Anti-balaka communal war.

name: CPC Offensive on Bangui
description: Coalition of Patriots for Change offensive led by Francois Bozize against the Touadera government, repelled by Russian Wagner Group and Rwandan reinforcements.

name: Lord's Resistance Army in Central Africa
description: Westward dispersion of Joseph Kony's LRA into the DRC, CAR and South Sudan after Operation Lightning Thunder, hunted by Ugandan, US and AU regional forces.

name: Operation Lightning Thunder
description: Joint UPDF-FARDC-SPLA assault on the LRA's Garamba sanctuary in northeastern DRC that scattered Kony's forces across three countries.

name: Bakassi Conflict
description: Sporadic armed clashes between Nigeria and Cameroon over the Bakassi peninsula, resolved by the 2002 ICJ ruling and the 2006 Greentree Agreement.

name: Anglophone Crisis
description: Armed insurgency by Ambazonian separatists in Cameroon's Anglophone Northwest and Southwest regions against Yaounde's francophone-dominated state.

name: Boko Haram in Cameroon and Chad
description: Spillover of the Boko Haram and ISWAP insurgencies from northeast Nigeria into Cameroon's Far North and the Lake Chad basin of Chad and Niger.

name: Chadian Civil War 1965-1979
description: FROLINAT-led northern Muslim insurgency against the Christian-southern Tombalbaye regime, with successive French Operation Bison and Tacaud interventions.

name: Chadian-Libyan War
description: Series of campaigns in northern Chad over the Aouzou Strip culminating in Hissene Habre's 'Toyota War' victories at Fada and Ouadi Doum and the Libyan withdrawal.

name: Toyota War
description: Final phase of the Chadian-Libyan War in which Chadian forces in Toyota technicals routed the Libyan army from northern Chad.

name: Chadian Civil War 2005-2010
description: Sudan-backed Chadian rebel offensives on N'Djamena (Battle of N'Djamena 2008) and Am Dam, ended by the Chad-Sudan rapprochement.

name: Battle of N'Djamena
description: Three-day battle in the Chadian capital between government forces and the UFDD coalition, repelled with French logistical support.

name: Chadian Conflict against FACT 2021
description: Front for Change and Concord in Chad offensive from Libya into northern Chad in which President Idriss Deby was killed.

name: UNITA Insurgency
description: Jonas Savimbi's UNITA insurgency phase of the Angolan Civil War, sustained by South African and US support until his death and the 2002 Luena memorandum.

name: Cuban Intervention in Angola
description: Sixteen-year Cuban expeditionary deployment of up to 55,000 troops in support of the MPLA government, including Operation Carlota and Cuito Cuanavale.

name: Mayombe Insurgency
description: MPLA's northern front in Cabinda during the Angolan War of Independence, operating out of Congo-Brazzaville's Mayombe forest.

name: Eastern Front (Angola)
description: MPLA and UNITA offensives from Zambia into eastern Angola during the independence war, countered by Portugal's Operacao Lambada.

name: Cassinga Raid
description: SADF airborne raid on the SWAPO base at Cassinga in southern Angola that killed hundreds, contested as either a military operation or a refugee massacre.

name: Operation Reindeer
description: Multi-pronged SADF operation against SWAPO bases in southern Angola including Cassinga and Chetequera.

name: Operation Protea
description: Major SADF mechanised incursion into Cunene province against SWAPO and FAPLA that destroyed Soviet equipment and killed a senior Soviet adviser.

name: Operation Askari
description: SADF cross-border operation against SWAPO and FAPLA in Cunene that produced the Lusaka Accords disengagement.

name: Operation Modular
description: SADF and UNITA defeat of the FAPLA offensive against Mavinga on the Lomba River, the prelude to Cuito Cuanavale.

name: Operation Hooper
description: SADF follow-on offensive against the FAPLA Tumpo Triangle bridgehead east of Cuito Cuanavale.

name: Operation Packer
description: Final SADF assault on the Tumpo Triangle east of Cuito Cuanavale, ending the conventional phase of the Border War.

name: Bicesse Accords Collapse
description: Resumption of full-scale war after UNITA's rejection of the 1992 election results, including the 55-day Battle of Huambo and the siege of Kuito.

name: Battle of Huambo 1993
description: Fifty-five-day urban battle in which UNITA captured Angola's second city from FAA forces.

name: Siege of Kuito
description: Eighteen-month UNITA siege of the FAA-held provincial capital of Bie, one of the deadliest urban episodes of the Angolan Civil War.

name: Burundian Civil War Spillover into DRC
description: Cross-border operations of CNDD-FDD and Palipehutu-FNL from sanctuaries in South Kivu during the Burundian Civil War, entangled with the Congo Wars.

name: Banyamulenge Revolt
description: Rwandan-backed Banyamulenge Tutsi rising against Mobutu's expulsion order, the immediate trigger of the First Congo War.

name: RCD Insurgency
description: Rwandan- and Ugandan-sponsored Rally for Congolese Democracy rebellion against Laurent-Desire Kabila that occupied much of eastern Congo during the Second Congo War.

name: MLC Insurgency
description: Jean-Pierre Bemba's Ugandan-backed Movement for the Liberation of the Congo offensive in Equateur and Orientale during the Second Congo War.

name: Bemba Wars
description: Bemba expansion out of the Lunda fringe across the plateau between the Luangwa and Lake Bangweulu during the era of long-distance ivory and slave trade.

name: Ovimbundu Trade Wars
description: Inter-kingdom warfare among the Ovimbundu plateau states of Bie, Bailundo, Wambu and others as they competed over the Benguela caravan trade with the interior.

name: Tippu Tip's Conquests
description: Swahili-Arab slave and ivory empire-building by Hamed bin Mohammed (Tippu Tip) across Manyema and the upper Congo, eventually overthrown in the Congo Arab War.

name: Battle of Nyangwe
description: Dhanis's capture of the Swahili-Arab slaving capital of Nyangwe on the Lualaba during the Congo Arab War.

name: Battle of Kasongo 1893
description: Force Publique storming of Tippu Tip's stronghold at Kasongo, the centrepiece victory of the Congo Arab War.

name: Operation Carlota
description: Cuban airlift and sealift of expeditionary forces to Angola in November 1975 that decisively reinforced the MPLA against the FNLA-South African intervention.

name: Mai-Mai Insurgencies
description: Constellation of Congolese community self-defence militias raised first against the AFDL and then against the RCD, M23 and Rwandan-backed groups in the Kivus and northern Katanga.

name: Kibati Rebellion
description: Force Publique mutiny at Luluabourg in February 1944 followed by Kibati and Jadotville miners' strikes, the largest wartime unrest in the Belgian Congo.

name: Leopoldville Riots
description: Days of rioting in the Belgian Congo's capital that broke Belgian confidence in continued colonial rule and triggered the rapid timetable to independence.

name: Force Publique Mutiny
description: Mutiny of the Force Publique at Thysville and Leopoldville days after independence that triggered the Belgian military intervention and the Congo Crisis.

name: South Kasai Secession
description: Albert Kalonji's Luba-led secessionist mini-state in the Kasai diamond fields, defeated by Lumumba's ANC and ended by Mobutu in 1962.

name: Operation Morthor
description: UN ONUC offensive against Katangese gendarmes in Elisabethville that bogged down at Jadotville and led to the death of Secretary-General Hammarskjold.

name: Siege of Jadotville
description: Five-day stand of an Irish ONUC company against Katangese gendarmes and mercenaries during Operation Morthor.

name: Operation Grandslam
description: Final UN offensive that ended the Katangese secession by capturing Elisabethville, Jadotville and Kolwezi.

name: Battle of Mbanza Mbata
description: Portuguese raid into Kongo's Mbata province during Governor Joao Correia de Sousa's brief war on Kongo.

name: Wagner Group in CAR
description: Russian Wagner Group deployment in support of the Touadera government, combining presidential protection, anti-rebel operations and resource extraction.
